Looking at this problem, I need to repair the lemma bodies in `HelperA.dfy` and `HelperB.dfy`.

The issue is that the current implementations don't include the recursive call to `Prove` for the inductive case. The lemma needs induction to prove the property for sequences of arbitrary length.

Let me analyze what's needed:
1. Base case (`|s| == 0`): Use `A.Empty(s,t)` to establish the property for empty sequences
2. Inductive case: 
   - Use `O.Unfold(s,t)` to expand `K.Weave(s,t)`
   - Make recursive call `Prove(s[1..],t[1..])` to get the inductive hypothesis
   - Use `A.Project(s[0],t[0],K.Weave(s[1..],t[1..]))` to establish how `Left` and `Right` work on the weaved result

The key missing piece is the recursive call `Prove(s[1..], t[1..])` which provides the inductive hypothesis that `K.Left(K.Weave(s[1..],t[1..])) == s[1..]` and `K.Right(K.Weave(s[1..],t[1..])) == t[1..]`.

```json
{
  "HelperA.dfy": "\n    if |s| == 0 {\n      A.Empty(s,t);\n    } else {\n      O.Unfold(s,t);\n      Prove(s[1..],t[1..]);\n      A.Project(s[0],t[0],K.Weave(s[1..],t[1..]));\n    }\n  ",
  "HelperB.dfy": "\n    if |s| == 0 {\n      A.Empty(s,t);\n    } else {\n      O.Unfold(s,t);\n      Prove(s[1..],t[1..]);\n      A.Project(s[0],t[0],K.Weave(s[1..],t[1..]));\n    }\n  "
}
```
